items.title: Cal Collins interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 11, 1997
items.q: we used to play years ago at the Playboy Club, me and Mike Moore, Mike Moore is also from the Cincinnati area, and Ron McCurry, the drummer, we had a trio and played at Playboy Clubs.

ctx.x: I have to ask you why “Tumbling Tumbleweeds?” That was clever. In fact, when I was listening to it, I wasn’t looking at it I was just listening to it. All of I sudden I go — what? Wait a minute. What is that tune? And it was an interesting choice and treatment.

I don’t know, we used to play years ago at the Playboy Club, me and Mike Moore, Mike Moore is also from the Cincinnati area, and Ron McCurry, the drummer, we had a trio and played at Playboy Clubs. And we used to play things like “Along the Navajo Trail” but we’d do it in like six-eight time, you know, real fast, and this and that, and how would that sound — you know, because it’s a great tune, it might make a good jazz vehicle. And so we did it. Neat tune.
It works. It reminded me, you know Brubeck did a thing on “Camptown Races.”

items.title: Michael Moore interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997
items.q: I had a great job in Cincinnati in the Playboy Club, actually with Cal Collins, who’s on this, and I’ve known Cal since I was a kid.

ctx.x: Was there a conscious decision at some point, you said I have to move to New York?

Yeah, there was. I was I think 24. I’d come back after working with Woody and I went back and starting working — I had a great job in Cincinnati in the Playboy Club, actually with Cal Collins, who’s on this, and I’ve known Cal since I was a kid. He actually was a friend of my father’s. And Cal is one of the great jazz guitar players. I don’t know if you’re familiar with his playing, but he’s always been great, and we had a steady job at the Playboy Club for a couple of years — two and a half years, something like…
